title: Syntomic composition and smooth inputs
statement: Call a map $T\to E$ syntomic if it is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and every fibre $E\otimes_T\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field]. For commutative ring maps $R\to S\to T$, if both maps are syntomic, so is their composite $R\to T$. Every smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] is syntomic. Every ring map $R\to S$ for which $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] is syntomic.

proof.text: First prove the relative-chart calculation used below. Suppose $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ and $B=A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]/(h_1,\ldots,h_d)$ are relative global complete intersections. Lift each $h_j$ to $h'_j\in R[x,y]$. Successive quotient universal properties give $B\cong R[x,y]/(f,h')$. Fix $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $V=B\otimes_R k\ne0$, where $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and put $U=A\otimes_R k$. Base change preserves the two relative presentations, so $\dim U=n-c$ and every nonempty fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}V\to\operatorname{Spec}U$ has dimension $m-d$. Here the fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}V\to\operatorname{Spec}U$ over $\mathfrak u$, as a subspace, is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(V\otimes_U\kappa(\mathfrak u))$ by the fibre/spectrum homeomorphism, so these topological fibres are the spectra of the tensor-product fibre rings. The nonzero ring $V$ has a prime; its image in $\operatorname{Spec}U$ has nonempty fibre. Thus $n\ge c$ and $m\ge d$. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$), and $U$ is a finite type $k$-algebra, hence Noetherian. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}V\to\operatorname{Spec}U$ is finite type by the displayed presentation. Apply the source-dimension/fibre bound to obtain $\dim V\le(n-c)+(m-d)$. The polynomial-quotient lower bound applied to $V=k[x,y]/(\bar f,\bar h')$ gives $\dim V\ge n+m-c-d$. Equality proves that the combined presentation is relative global complete intersection. Zero fibres impose no condition; if $B=0$ all fibres are zero.

source.place: Tag 00SZ (lemma-composition-syntomic), proof of (2); Tag 00OM (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-total), in its scheme form cited by the dimension-bound node; Tag 00S9, paragraph after definition-lci-field, for the opposite dimension bound.

proof.text: Now let $R\to S\xrightarrow{\psi}T$ be syntomic and fix a prime $\mathfrak q\subset T$, with $\mathfrak s=\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Apply the syntomic-at-prime relative-presentation lemma to $R\to S$ at $\mathfrak s$ and to $S\to T$ at $\mathfrak q$. Its finite-presentation hypothesis holds with the element $1$. Its local flatness hypothesis follows from the flat-map local criterion. For its fibre hypothesis, the definition of a local complete intersection supplies a principal global-complete-intersection neighbourhood of the fibre prime $\ker(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak s\cap R)\to\kappa(\mathfrak s))$, respectively $\ker(T\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak s)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q))$. Consequently choose $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak s$ and $h\in T\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $R\to S_g$ and $S\to T_h$ are relative global complete intersections.

source.place: Tag 00SZ (lemma-composition-syntomic), proof of (1), applying Tag 00SY (lemma-syntomic); definition of syntomic in Tag 00SL and of lci fibres in Tag 00S9.

proof.text: Write $a=\psi(g)h\in T$. Since neither factor belongs to $\mathfrak q$, $a\notin\mathfrak q$. Base change of the relative presentation for $S\to T_h$ along $S\to S_g$ gives a relative global complete intersection $S_g\to S_g\otimes_ST_h$. Localization base change and transitivity identify its target with $T_a$: to invert $\psi(g)$ and $h$ is exactly to invert their product, with the canonical maps agreeing on $T$. Apply the complete presentation-and-dimension calculation of step 1 to $R\to S_g\to T_a$. It follows that $R\to T_a$ is a relative global complete intersection.

For every $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}T$, step 3 supplies $a\notin\mathfrak q$ and a relative-global-complete-intersection chart $R\to T_a$. Thus these $D(a)$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}T$. The spectrum's quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover $D(a_1),\ldots,D(a_r)$, and the basic-open/unit-ideal criterion gives coefficients $b_i\in T$ with $\sum b_i a_i=1$. Apply relative-CI principal-cover syntomic gluing: $R\to T$ is flat, finitely presented, and has lci residue-field fibres, exactly the three required properties. If $T=0$, use the empty cover and $0=1$, which the same gluing statement explicitly allows.

source.place: Tag 00SZ (lemma-composition-syntomic), final paragraph; Tag 00SO (lemma-local-syntomic); Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), quasi-compactness and standard-open covers.

proof.text: For the smooth clause, first take a standard smooth presentation $A\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$, $n\ge c$, as in the standard-smooth definition. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, standard-smooth base change gives a standard smooth presentation of $A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with the same numbers of variables and relations. At each point of this fibre spectrum the standard-smooth-over-a-field dimension theorem gives dimension $n-c$. If the fibre ring is nonzero its spectrum is nonempty, by existence of a maximal ideal. The dimension-supremum theorem therefore gives global dimension $n-c$. This is precisely the condition for the original displayed presentation to be a relative global complete intersection; zero fibres require nothing.

source.place: Tag 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth), assertion (7), and its proof by fibre base change and dimension; Tag 0B7I (lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions).

proof.text: Let $R\to S$ be smooth. At every prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$ the locally-standard-smooth lemma supplies $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that $S_g$ is standard smooth over $R$. By step 5, each such $R\to S_g$ is a relative global complete intersection. As in step 4, select a finite standard-open subcover, obtain a unit-ideal relation, and apply relative-CI principal-cover syntomic gluing. This proves all three syntomic conditions for $R\to S$, including finite presentation globally. The empty spectrum is covered by the same empty-cover case.

source.place: Tag 00TA (lemma-smooth-syntomic), local standard-smooth cover and final paragraph; Tag 00SO (lemma-local-syntomic).

proof.text: Finally, suppose $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale. The affine etale/ring-map criterion states that $S$ is finitely presented over $R$, $H_1(L_{S/R})=0$ and $\Omega_{S/R}=0$. The zero module is finite projective, being the free module on the empty basis. These are exactly the three clauses in the definition of a smooth ring map. Thus $R\to S$ is smooth, and step 6 makes it syntomic.

source.place: Tag 00U1 (definition-etale), with Tag 02GJ (lemma-etale-characterize); Tag 00T2 (definition-smooth). This uses the defining etale conditions directly rather than the stronger standard-smooth conclusion of Tag 00U9.
